title: OAuth / OIDC / WebAuthn Advanced
description: Identity federation, token validation, and passkey fallback risks.

attacks.name: PKCE downgrade
attacks.desc: Dropping a PKCE challenge or accepting a weaker flow can allow interception of an authorization code.
attacks.prevention: Require PKCE for public clients and reject authorization requests or token exchanges missing the expected challenge.

attacks.name: OAuth mix-up attack
attacks.desc: OAuth mix-up confuses which identity provider issued a response when a client supports multiple providers.
attacks.prevention: Bind the authorization response to the chosen identity provider and verify issuer and state before accepting tokens.

attacks.name: Device flow phishing
attacks.desc: An attacker can trick a user into entering a device-flow code that authorizes the attacker's session.
attacks.prevention: Explain device-code approvals clearly, limit code lifetime, and require users to verify the requesting app and context.

attacks.name: Dynamic client registration abuse
attacks.desc: Permissive dynamic registration can allow an attacker-controlled OAuth client with unsafe redirect behavior.
attacks.prevention: Restrict client registration to trusted administrators or enforce strict redirect URI and client metadata policy.

attacks.name: OIDC id_token validation flaws
attacks.desc: An OIDC client must validate the ID token's issuer, audience, signature, expiry, and nonce where applicable.

attacks.name: Implicit flow token leak
attacks.notes: Token in URL fragment exposed to scripts or browser state
attacks.desc: Implicit-flow tokens in URL fragments can be exposed to client-side scripts or browser state; fragments are not normally sent in Referer headers.

attacks.name: redirect_uri wildcard abuse
attacks.desc: Broad redirect URI matching can send authorization responses to an attacker-controlled subdomain or path.

attacks.name: Token replay
attacks.desc: Reusing a consumed authorization code or token can create duplicate access if replay protections fail.

attacks.name: Scope escalation
attacks.desc: A client or resource server may grant more permissions than consented when scopes are not validated consistently.

attacks.name: WebAuthn bypass
attacks.desc: WebAuthn assertions must match the expected origin and relying-party identifier.

attacks.name: Passkey downgrade
attacks.desc: A weak fallback path can bypass the protection provided by passkeys.

attacks.name: Account linking takeover
attacks.desc: Linking identities by an unverified email address can attach an attacker account to a victim account.
